data.title: SPACCircle Acquisition Corp. Announces the Separate Trading of its Class A Ordinary Shares, Warrants and Rights, Commencing November 10, 2026
data.description:
Sacramento, CA, Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SPACCircle Acquisition Corp. (the “Company”) announced today that, commencing November 10, 2026, holders of the units sold in the Company’s initial public offering may elect to separately trade the Company’s Class A ordinary shares, warrants and rights included in the units. The Class A ordinary shares, warrants and rights that are separated will trade on the Nasdaq Global Market under the symbols “SCQC,” “SCQCW” and “SCQCR,” respectively. Those units not separated will continue to trade on the Nasdaq Global Market under the symbol “SCQCU.”

The units were initially offered by the Company in an underwritten offering. D. Boral Capital LLC acted as sole book-running manager of the offering. Copies of the prospectus relating to the offering may be obtained from D. Boral Capital LLC, 590 Madison Avenue, 39th Floor, New York, NY 10022, by email at dbccapitalmarkets@dboralcapital.com, or by telephone at (212) 970-5150.

This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy the securities of the Company, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction.

About SPACCircle Acquisition Corp.

The Company was formed for the purpose of effecting a merger, amalgamation, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses. It may pursue an initial business combination target in any business or industry.

This press release may include, and oral statements made from time to time by representatives of the Company may include, “forward-looking statements” within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. Such forward-looking statements are based on the beliefs of management, as well as assumptions made by, and information currently available to, the Company’s management. Actual results could differ materially from those contemplated by the forward-looking statements as a result of certain factors detailed in the Company’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”). All subsequent written or oral forward-looking statements attributable to us or persons acting on our behalf are qualified in their entirety by this paragraph. Forward-looking statements are subject to numerous conditions, many of which are beyond the control of the Company, including those set forth in the Risk Factors section of the Company’s registration statement and prospectus for the Company’s initial public offering filed with the SEC. data.title: LifeMD Reschedules Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Release and Conference Call to November 12, 2026
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LifeMD, Inc. , a leading provider of virtual primary care and pharmacy services, today announced that the Company has rescheduled its third quarter 2026 earnings release and conference call to Thursday, November 12, 2026.

LifeMD expects to issue its third quarter 2026 earnings press release on or around 4:05 p.m. Eastern time on Thursday, November 12, 2026 followed by the conference call at 4:30 p.m. Eastern time. Information for the rescheduled conference call is as follows:

Conference Call & Webcast Details

Date:Thursday, November 12th
Time:4:30 p.m. Eastern time
Toll-Free Dial-In:(877) 270-2148
International Dial-In:+1 (412) 902-6510
Conference ID:LifeMD, Inc. Third Quarter 2026 Results
Live & Archived Webcast:Link

About LifeMD, Inc.

LifeMD® is a leading virtual care company making high-quality healthcare more accessible, convenient, and affordable. Through its vertically integrated platform, LifeMD connects patients with a 50-state affiliated medical group, laboratory services, a state-of-the-art nationwide pharmacy with home delivery, and a U.S.-based patient care center. Together, these capabilities support care across more than 200 conditions, including primary care, men's and women's health, weight management, and hormone therapy. For more information, please visit LifeMD.com.

data.title: Uber's Robo Push — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Ty Roush

Here's Uber's big bet: Its customer network will provide an edge in the ultra-competitive robo-taxi market.

The numbers? The ride-hailing giant expects to have 700 driverless vehicles on its platform by the end of 2026 and more than 2,000 by the end of 2027. That's not all. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi aims to expand that fleet to tens of thousands of autonomous vehicles by 2030. He also plans to invest as much as $10 billion, including $7.5 billion to build its own fleet and $2.5 billion in equity stakes in self-driving technology companies.

The strategy all hinges on keeping robo-taxis super busy. Autonomous vehicles on its U.S. network complete 30% more trips per day than those operating outside its platform, according to William Blair. Uber estimates a 30% increase in paid trips would reduce fixed costs per ride by about 23%, potentially improving returns for fleet operators even after paying Uber a share of fares.

Uber's growing delivery business could provide another avenue for autonomous expansion. Third-quarter delivery gross bookings reached $28.5 billion, compared with $29.5 billion for mobility, narrowing the gap to about $1 billion from $1.8 billion a year earlier.

But competition poses a growing threat. Autonomous-vehicle developers could bypass Uber's platform and offer rides directly to customers. Alphabet's Waymo plans to end its exclusive partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta in 2028, allowing customers to book driverless rides through its own app. Let the robo-wars begin.

Write to Ty Roush at tyler.roush@barrons.com

Last Week

AI On the Run?

It took Wall Street two days after the midterms to figure out that the Democrats might not be good for artificial intelligence. Then, after the Thursday crash, there was the inevitable tech comeback. For the week: the S&P 500, down 2.68%; the Dow, minus 0.94%; and the Nasdaq Composite, down 3.37%. Pass the Prozac.

Speaking of Armageddon...

Per The Wall Street Journal, Paul Singer's hedge fund, Elliott Investment Management, cautioned in October that "alarm bells" are "warning of a substantial" market selloff. One alarm: some Roaring '20s-like froth. Alarm No. 2: the so-called "circular investments" between the AI model firms and infrastructure AI guys.

Gee, Thanks, Tim Cook

Apple beat analyst projections for its fiscal fourth quarter, but the stock was whacked earlier in the week. Freshman CEO John Ternus was left to explain why gross margins declined (memory pricing!) and why relief wasn't necessarily in sight. KeyBanc analyst Brandon Nispel: "We think Apple is at the point of extreme overvaluation."

Money for Nothing

In the U.S. Senate race in Cameron County, Texas, home of Elon Musk's SpaceX, James Talarico slam-dunked Musk-backed Ken Paxton by some 38 percentage points. President Trump won the county by six points in 2024. As Musk's ex, Grimes, once sang, "Nothing lasts forever."

Next Week

Monday 11/9

Nearly 90% of S&P 500 index companies have reported third-quarter results, and year-over-year earnings growth is about 29% so?far. That's actually a slight deceleration from the second quarter's 33% jump, and apparently not enough for investors, as the S&P 500 is down 3.6% since the beginning of October. This week, Constellation Energy and Skydance release earnings on Monday; Applied Materials and Cisco Systems announce their results on Thursday.

Tuesday 11/10

The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the consumer price index for October. Economists forecast a 0.3% month-over-month increase, following a 0.6% jump in September. The core CPI is expected to rise 0.2%, one-tenth of a percentage point less than in?September. The BLS won't release year-over-year statistics because there was no October 2025 reference-period data collected due to the government shutdown from Oct. 1 to Nov. 12 of last year.

Thursday 11/12

The National Association of Realtors reports existing-home sales for October. Consensus estimate is for a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.85 million homes sold, about 3% less than in September.
